title: Compatibility Contracts for Fallback Variant Matrix and Tokenizer/KV Edgecases
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: As part of Smart Routing we need deterministic, machine-readable compatibility guarantees for fallback model variants. Current artifact set is fragmented across ad-hoc CSVs and PR comments. This ticket creates a compatibility 'contract' that covers tokenizer behavior, max-context semantics, KV cache compatibility, and common tooling interfaces (streaming, function-calling, structured outputs).

Goals:
- Define explicit compatibility assertions for each model variant (tokenizer id, byte-level behavior, pad/truncation semantics, context-length semantics, kv-cache key format, and tool-calling hooks).
- Produce a canonical matrix (CSV + JSON contract) and a maintenance playbook for updates when models change.
- Add automated sanity checks in CI that validate tokenizer equivalence for known fallback pairings and flag behavior drift.

Deliverables:
- compatibility_contracts/compatibility_matrix.csv (authoritative source for routing decisions)
- an automated CI job (ci/compatibility-sanity) that runs differential tokenization tests and KV roundtrip smoke tests
- maintenance playbook and owner rotation for the matrix

Acceptance criteria:
1) Matrix covers all active fallback pairings referenced by smart-routing policies and is consumable by the routing service.
2) CI job triggers a failure on tokenizer token-level divergence > 0.5% on the canonical test corpus, or on KV roundtrip failures.
3) Owners and update cadence documented; add a console view link in the PRD for visibility.

Links:
- PRD: https://docs.internal.redwood/prd/smart-routing-fallbacks
- Tokenizer test corpus: https://storage.redwood/test-corpora/fallback-tokenizer-corpus-v2.txt
- Example upstream issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/7512
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial spike completed. Marco validated tokenization differences between primary and two planned fallback variants for en-US and en-GB; identified canonical normalization mismatch for one variant.
2026-03-04: Decided to include both raw tokenizer IDs and normalized byte-level fingerprints in the contract. This lets routing accept fallbacks when a lightweight normalization shim is available.
2026-03-07: Prototype CI job added in ci/compatibility-sanity; currently runs tokenization diffs for 50 sample prompts. Failing cases logged to team Slack channel #eng-compatibility.

2026-03-10: Design review with PM and Runtime leads. Agreed to the following trade-offs: do not block rollout for minor tokenizer differences <0.5% if a shim is available; block for KV-format incompatibilities. Added label guidance for routing rules (prefer exact tokenizer matches for P0 customers).
comments: PM note (Lina Gomez): Need visibility in Console before Dedicated go-live for EU region. Please add a dashboard tile linking to the matrix and recent CI run results.
Design input (Samir Rao): Consider adding a compact visual diff in the Console that highlights canonical tokenization mismatches per prompt example.
Security (Priya Shah): KV format checks must include proof that no secret material is leaked during the roundtrip tests. Use mocked keys in CI and log only hashes.
review_feedback: Runtime lead (Evan Brooks): Suggest adding a lightweight runtime compatibility layer that can translate a small set of KV keys for known variants to avoid hard fallbacks.
SDK lead (Hannah Kim): We should expose a validator endpoint that SDKs can call to check a customer's model pairing before routing is applied.
QA (Diego Fernandez): Increase tokenization sample set to include edgecases: unicode emoji sequences, CJK, and ligatures.
